item.title: [Due today] From 4 November every default user can create agent blueprints unless 'Users can create agent blueprints' is set to No
item.description:
A default-on permission for every member user to create a new kind of workload identity widens the app-registration surface that consent-phishing and persistence techniques already abuse, and tenants that locked down app registration are not covered by that setting.

Entra · deadline 2026-11-04 · Decide before 4 November: set 'Users can create agent blueprints' to No unless there is a business case, keep Agent ID Developer as the delegated path, and add agent blueprint creation by non-admins to the app-registration detections.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due today] Entra stops auto-granting AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agent blueprints from 4 November; app-only agents that create their own identities need explicit admin consent or get 403
item.description:
Until now every agent blueprint could mint agent identities without any admin approval and without a visible grant. After the change that authority becomes an auditable, revocable app-role assignment, so the grant itself becomes something to monitor.

Entra · deadline 2026-11-04 · Before 4 November, filter the Entra audit log on ApplicationManagement / Add Service Principal where the initiator is an Application and the target an agent identity; grant AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager explicitly (from 16 October) only to the blueprints that need it, and alert on new grants of it afterwards.

item.title: [New] Eight permissions become grantable in the Microsoft Graph service principal: HardDeletionSetting.ReadWrite.Enable and seven ResourcePolicy* scopes
item.description:
A permission that appears in the service principal is consentable in every tenant from that day, before any documentation exists; the ReadWrite.All scopes write tenant-wide resource policy, and a consent to them is an administrative change by an app.

Graph · Add the sixteen GUIDs to the consent watch list and alert on any grant of the ReadWrite.All scopes or of HardDeletionSetting.ReadWrite.Enable.

item.description:

item.title: [New] Reminder: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retires from 1 February 2027; users with only SMS or voice get one last use, then must register a passkey
item.description:
Every user whose only second factor is SMS or voice hits a forced passkey registration at sign-in from 1 February 2027; that registration flow is a phishing and help-desk social-engineering target, and SMS/voice MFA stays a SIM-swap risk until it is gone.

Entra · Query authentication-method registration for users whose only method is SMS or voice, move them to passkeys or another method before 1 February 2027, or configure a customer-managed telecom provider if SMS/voice must stay; brief the help desk.

item.title: [Message Center] MC1528000 Microsoft Entra ID: Reminder to migrate from Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication
item.description:
Microsoft Entra ID will retire Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication starting February 1, 2027. Organizations must migrate users to passkeys or other methods, or configure a customer-managed telecom provider before then to avoid sign-in disruptions. SMS and voice are vulnerable to attacks; passkeys are recommended.
